structure.intro: ENEC and its subsidiaries, who owns them, and the bodies that oversee Barakah.
structure.diagramNote: Simplified. ENEC Consulting ownership is not confirmed in public sources.
structure.diagramAlt: ADQ owns 100% of ENEC. ENEC owns 82% of ENEC Operations and of ENEC Commercial; KEPCO owns 18% of each. ENEC Consulting is an ENEC subsidiary.

enec.name: ENEC
enec.role: Owner and developer of Barakah; investment arm; leads international partnerships. Established December 2009.

enec-ops.name: ENEC Operations
enec-ops.role: Operates and maintains Barakah Units 1-4 and holds the four FANR operating licences. Still registered and licensed as Nawah.

enec-com.name: ENEC Commercial
enec-com.role: Holds project finance, the 60-year power purchase agreement with EWEC and the DoE generation licence.

enec-con.name: ENEC Consulting
enec-con.role: Advisory arm for countries starting nuclear programmes, launched 15 January 2025.

structure.oversightIntro: Kafa'a is not a regulatory channel. Regulators appear only as sources and, where ENEC chooses, as observers of aggregate reports.

fanr.name: FANR
fanr.body: Independent regulator for safety, security, radiation protection and safeguards. Certifies ROs and SROs under FANR-REG-17.

iaea.name: IAEA
iaea.body: Safeguards and peer-review missions (INIR, OSART, EPREV); source of SSG-75 staffing and qualification guidance.

ead.name: EAD
ead.body: Environmental regulator; partner on the 500,000-coral programme.

ad-doe.name: Abu Dhabi DoE
ad-doe.body: Generation licence and the Clean Energy Certificate scheme.

ncema.name: NCEMA
ncema.body: National emergency authority for off-site planning; supervises national Barakah exercises.
